claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is substitution of 3–5 at% of one or more refractory elements in HfNbTaTiZr with Al.
A 3–5 at% Al addition to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a continuous alumina scale at 800 °C in air.
The alumina scale formed on the Al-modified alloy will be adherent.
A dense, continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale can protect alloys against high-temperature oxidation because of its thermodynamic stability and low ionic diffusivities.
Al has sufficiently high oxygen affinity and favorable oxide-formation free energy to oxidize preferentially in the proposed HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The proposed alumina layer will inhibit further oxygen ingress into Al-modified HfNbTaTiZr.
Hf can promote alumina-scale adhesion by acting as a reactive element and forming Hf-rich particles at oxide grain boundaries.
The 3–5 at% Al addition will leave the bulk cast microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical properties largely unchanged.
The Al-modified alloy will show reduced or eliminated pesting relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
The Al-modified alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility after oxidation exposure.
The Al-modified alloy will retain a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr pests during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
Minor Al additions can preserve mechanical performance despite Al's possible effects on phase stability and microstructural evolution.

contradictions.description: The conditions and experiment describe oxidation exposure as occurring under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹, whereas the boundary assigns those strain rates to high-temperature mechanical tests. It is therefore unclear whether oxidation is performed under load or whether loading occurs only in subsequent testing.
